title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Page 31 of the 'Longue Marche' manuscript, numbered page 62 of the archive file. It belongs to Grothendieck's sequence of section-conjecture statements (Conjectures A, B, B').

Setting from the previous page. Grothendieck defines 'courbes / revêtements de Poincaré' over an algebraically closed field Kbar. These are pro-universal (étale, possibly ramified) covers of hyperbolic algebraic curves, taken up to commensurability: two curves U and V give isomorphic Poincaré covers iff some finite étale cover of one is isomorphic to some finite étale cover of the other. A Poincaré cover \mathcal U has a 'completion' \hat{\mathcal U} = \mathfrak X. This is presumably the projective limit of the smooth compactifications of the finite levels, equivalently their Kbar-points including cusps. It is set up so that every semilinear automorphism of (\mathcal U, Kbar) acts on it, even one not inducing the identity on Kbar.

Conjecture B'.
- Let K be finitely generated over Q, or over a cyclotomic field (possibly of infinite degree), or more generally....
- Let Γ = Gal(Kbar/K) act continuously on \mathcal U, compatibly with its action on Kbar. This gives an action on \mathfrak X.
- Claim: the subgroup Γ^0 = ker(χ: Γ → \hat Z^*), the kernel of the cyclotomic character, i.e. Gal(Kbar/K(μ_∞)), has exactly one fixed point on \mathfrak X.

Difference from Conjecture B. B assumed that Γ normalizes a profinite group π acting discontinuously on \mathcal U with \mathcal U/π an algebraic (ramified) cover of a curve V over Kbar. In that case a Γ-action amounts to a section of the extension 1→π→E→Γ→1 attached to a curve over K, and B is the 'fixed-point' form of the section conjecture (cusps allowed, uniqueness included). B' removes the normalization hypothesis. Γ may then act only by 'virtual' automorphisms, i.e. through the commensurability class, the way Galois acts on adelic Shimura/modular towers.

Why Γ^0 rather than Γ. In the typical example of such a non-normalizing action (the modular tower), elements with nontrivial cyclotomic character act through det = χ. They permute geometric components and act like Hecke correspondences, so they need not fix anything. Only Γ^0 can be expected to have a fixed point.

The next page applies the conjectures to models U_S → S and fibre-product diagrams of fundamental-group extensions.
errors: The conjecture is stated for K finitely generated over a cyclotomic field, including Q(μ_∞) = Q^ab. Even for K finitely generated over Q, the group Γ^0 = G_{K(μ_∞)} is the absolute Galois group of a field containing all roots of unity. Such fields lie outside the Kummer-faithful setting of present anabelian theorems.

G_{Q^ab} has cohomological dimension 1, i.e. it is projective, and by Shafarevich's conjecture it is free. So for a curve over Q^ab itself every extension splits and sections abound. The 'existence' half of a section conjecture over such fields is doubtful or false. Uniqueness over K(μ_∞) would also need an injectivity of Kummer maps that is not available there. Grothendieck's extension to cyclotomic base fields, and the claim of existence AND uniqueness for Γ^0, is therefore at best unproven and plausibly too optimistic, at least as stated over K = Q(μ_∞).
The 'completion' \hat{\mathcal U} is not defined precisely on this page. Whether the fixed point is meant in the profinite limit of points, including cusps, is left implicit.

ideas.what: Section conjecture formulated as a unique-fixed-point statement for a Galois action on the pro-universal cover (completion including cusps)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983); Esquisse d'un programme (allusion)

ideas.what: 'Courbes de Poincaré': pro-universal covers of hyperbolic curves over Kbar up to commensurability (common finite étale covers), with semilinear automorphisms not fixing Kbar
ideas.modern_name: commensurability classes of hyperbolic curves / profinite commensurator of π_1
ideas.usually_credited_to: commensurator viewpoint in later anabelian work, e.g. Mochizuki on Belyi-type and commensurator questions (unsure of exact attribution)

ideas.what: Conjecture B': Galois action on the Poincaré cover NOT normalizing any π (virtual / Hecke-type action); fixed point asserted only for the kernel of the cyclotomic character
ideas.modern_name: section conjecture for commensurator-valued Galois actions (Shimura/modular-tower type)
ideas.usually_credited_to: no known statement in the literature

ideas.what: Extension of anabelian conjectures to fields finitely generated over a cyclotomic field (not necessarily finite over Q)
ideas.usually_credited_to: open; partial anabelian results over Kummer-faithful fields (Mochizuki, Hoshi) exclude μ_∞

missed.claim: A strengthened section conjecture (B') for Galois actions on the commensurability class of a hyperbolic curve. Γ acts semilinearly on the pro-universal cover without normalizing any fundamental group. A unique fixed point is then predicted for Γ^0 = ker(cyclotomic character).
missed.quote: ici on ne suppose pas que l'action de Γ sur \mathcal U normalise l'action d'un groupe profini π
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a section-type conjecture for Hecke/commensurator-type actions, as on adelic modular and Shimura towers where det = χ. To my knowledge no such formulation appears in the section-conjecture literature (Stix, Pop, Mochizuki, Hoshi). It suggests studying profinite commensurators of surface groups as targets for Galois representations.

missed.claim: Using Γ^0 = ker χ signals a link between the cyclotomic character and the permutation of geometric components / Hecke action in non-normalizing actions, much as Galois acts on modular towers. This ties the section conjecture to arithmeticity of commensurators (Margulis-type phenomena) and to Shimura-curve towers.
missed.quote: il existe un point fixe et un seul de Γ^0 agissant sur \mathfrak X (Γ^0, noyau du caractère cyclotomique)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could frame a 'commensurator section conjecture' that distinguishes arithmetic (Shimura) curves, whose commensurator Galois actions are large, from generic ones.

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly extends the anabelian/section conjectures to bases finitely generated over cyclotomic fields of infinite degree.
missed.quote: Soit K un corps de type fini sur Q (ou sur un corps cyclotomique, ...)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Over Q^ab these statements are open and, for the existence part, likely false since G_{Q^ab} has cd 1. This is a documented over-optimism, or an unexplored regime, of anabelian geometry.

deep.surprise_reason: The page has a cuspidal fixed-point form of the section conjecture, which is known in spirit. It also has a variant B' for Galois actions on the commensurability class of the universal cover, restricted to the kernel of the cyclotomic character, and explicitly extended to bases over cyclotomic fields. To my knowledge this variant is not in the published record, and the commensurator/Hecke flavour is notable. Part of it is likely problematic over Q^ab.
